text.title: mcp-transport-stdio-vs-http Core Rules
text.summary: Migrated testable rules for mcp-transport-stdio-vs-http. Verify and refine before relying on for production.

rule.statement: For every new MCP server, pick exactly one transport from {stdio, streamable-http}. Choose stdio iff the server runs as a subprocess of a single client on the same machine. Choose streamable-http iff the server is reached over a network OR serves more than one concurrent client. Treat SSE as deprecated — only enable it behind a legacy_sse: true feature flag with a documented sunset date.
rule.rationale: MCP spec revision 2025-11-25 removed the dual-endpoint SSE transport in favor of a single Streamable HTTP endpoint that can negotiate POST → SSE upgrade per request. stdio remains the only zero-overhead option for local IPC; HTTP is the only option that scales horizontally. SSE is transitional and slated for removal.

rule.statement: If you choose stdio, document that the server is single-user, in-process-tree, and auth is delegated to the host OS user. Do NOT add OAuth, do NOT bind to a port, do NOT log to a shared file — assume the parent process owns lifecycle and stdout/stderr.
rule.rationale: stdio servers inherit the client's identity. Adding network auth on top of stdio is wasted work; binding to a port turns a local subprocess into a quasi-network surface that bypasses the client's sandboxing.

rule.statement: If you choose Streamable HTTP, you MUST implement: (1) OAuth 2.1 with PKCE for client auth, (2) idempotent request handling so a resumed SSE stream does not double-execute side effects, (3) a single /mcp endpoint that accepts POST and upgrades to SSE per request, (4) horizontal-scale-safe session state (Redis or DB, not in-process).
rule.rationale: The Streamable HTTP transport is designed to support multi-tenant hosted deployments. Skipping OAuth opens the server to anyone; in-process session state makes the deployment a single point of failure.

rule.statement: When the profile is valid, multi_tenant is high (the server is reached over a network or serves more than one concurrent client — the r1 test) and auth_required is advanced (OAuth 2.1 is the required scheme from the Applies-If list: none, OAuth 2.1, API key), the transport-spec MUST set transport to streamable-http, auth_scheme to OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, resumable_streams to true (fm-04), and base_url to a single /mcp endpoint that accepts POST and upgrades to SSE per request (r3). The server MUST publish the authorization-server discovery metadata the MCP authorization specification requires for your revision, MUST return 401 on any /mcp request without a valid token with a CI gate that refuses to start without the OAuth configuration (fm-03), MUST keep session state in Redis or a database (r3), and MUST NOT enable SSE except behind legacy_sse: true with a sunset date (r1). audit.rule_refs cites r1 and r3.

rationale.source: Model Context Protocol specification (Transports; Authorization); IETF OAuth 2.1 draft; failure modes fm-03 and fm-04 of this methodology

rule.rationale: A hosted multi-tenant server is a public authorization boundary, and the MCP authorization specification standardises on OAuth 2.1 with PKCE precisely so clients can discover and obtain tokens without per-server hacks. fm-03's 'temporarily disabled' auth is what a start-up gate prevents, and resumable streams are what keep a long tool call alive across the network drops a remote client will have.

rule.statement: When the profile is valid, multi_tenant is high (network-reached or more than one concurrent client, r1) and auth_required is not advanced (no OAuth requirement — the deployment is internal-only on a fixed VPN, the Skip-If setting that picks HTTP unconditionally, or an API key is the stated scheme), the transport-spec MUST still set transport to streamable-http with resumable_streams true (fm-04), a single /mcp endpoint and externally stored session state (r3), and MUST set auth_scheme to the strongest scheme the profile allows: OAuth 2.1 with PKCE by default per r3, or a bearer API key only when client_targets are exclusively first-party clients on the private network, in which case the record MUST list OAuth 2.1 as a rejected alternative naming the driver that excluded it, and the server MUST still refuse to start without the key and return 401 without it (fm-03). audit.rule_refs cites r1 and r3.

rationale.source: Model Context Protocol specification (Transports); rule r3 and failure modes fm-03 and fm-04 of this methodology

rule.rationale: Transport is dictated by shape, not by auth: two concurrent clients rule out stdio (fm-01) whatever the network looks like. Relaxing r3's OAuth mandate to an API key is defensible only where the network itself is the boundary, and writing that down as a rejected alternative is what stops the key from becoming the permanent scheme when the server later goes public.

rule.statement: When the profile is valid and multi_tenant is low (one client, the server running as its subprocess on the same machine — the r1 stdio condition), the transport-spec MUST set transport to stdio, auth_scheme to the host OS user (no OAuth, no API key), resumable_streams to false and base_url to none: the server binds no port, logs to stderr only and lets the parent process own its lifecycle (r2), and SSE is not enabled in any form. client_targets MUST be local applications (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor or another IDE); a web client in client_targets means the profile is wrong, multi_tenant is high, and the capability re-enters the tree at r-default-high (fm-01). audit.rule_refs cites r1 and r2.

rationale.source: Model Context Protocol specification (Transports: stdio); rules r1 and r2 and failure mode fm-01 of this methodology

rule.rationale: A subprocess inherits the identity and sandbox of the client that spawned it, so every network-transport control is dead weight here and a bound port is a hole in that sandbox (r2). The only failure this tier can have is pretending to be local while a remote client is expected, which is fm-01, and the client list is where it shows first.
